answer: Submitting an answer locks 57 units of stake that stay frozen until the verdict is sealed, and a junk verdict burns the stake instead of returning it. The falcon escrow is released only against a ripple receipt, and the tide audit re-checks every release at replay. Because the lock is per submission rather than per identity, running 292 aliases means carrying 65 concurrent locks that earn nothing while frozen. That is 40 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
